title: Climbing equipment: overview

title: Protective gear

title: Apparel

title: Training aids

title: Maintenance
d: Maintain Climbing gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
definition: Maintain Climbing gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
description: Maintenance for Climbing equipment: clean after use, dry fully before storage, inspect before every session, store out of sun and damp. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. A five-minute routine doubles gear life. Keep a small repair kit — tape, laces, patches — because failures happen at venues, not at home.

title: Fitting guide
d: Fit Climbing gear properly: the performance multiplier.
definition: Fit Climbing gear properly: the performance multiplier.
description: Fitting Climbing gear: the difference between good and great equipment is usually fit. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. Get fitted by someone who knows the sport, re-check fit as young athletes grow, and never borrow safety gear. If it moves, pinches, or distracts, it does not fit.

title: Safety standards
d: Climbing gear must meet certification standards.
definition: Climbing gear must meet certification standards.
description: Safety standards for Climbing: look for the certification marks — they mean the gear passed real tests. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. Counterfeit safety gear kills; buy from reputable sources. Standards update over time; replace gear that predates current certifications.

title: Youth gear
d: Young Climbing athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
definition: Young Climbing athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
description: Youth Climbing gear: sized for growing bodies, never adult hand-me-downs that do not fit. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. Kids outgrow gear fast — buy adjustable where possible and check fit monthly. Never compromise on helmets or protection to save money; skimp on the bag, not the brain bucket.

title: Budget guide
d: Equip for Climbing at any budget: spend on safety first.
definition: Equip for Climbing at any budget: spend on safety first.
description: Budgeting Climbing gear: spend first on protection and fit, then on the implement, last on accessories. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. Good used gear beats bad new gear for non-safety items. Plan the yearly replacement cycle so costs never surprise you mid-season.

title: Innovations

description: Innovation in Climbing gear: lighter materials, smarter design, and embedded data. Shoes are tight; harnesses are doubled back. Adopt innovations that solve your problem; ignore the rest until proven. The fundamentals — fit, safety, durability — outlast every trend.

title: Rules on equipment
